Parameters

These eight geometries have no case-specific calibration. Pressure, entrainment and loading are analytical estimates. Vessel and outlet always share one pressure. A compressible mass, momentum and energy balance is tried automatically when the low-Mach checks fail; conditions without an admissible estimate remain unavailable. “Unavailable” does not prove the hardware cannot work.

Model and geometry provenance

Revision 2 solves a CAD suction circuit with a common feeder and individual curved branches. Branch resistance determines unequal flow shares. British cases include eight separate bleed restrictions and a finite mixing-length pressure recovery. Main-bore and outlet areas enter the global mixing balance. The 0.75″ printed case retains its measured contraction, but its source solid is invalid and needs CAD repair before meshing.

λ = ṁpowder / ṁair   ·   powder mass fraction = λ / (1 + λ)
ṁair,out = ṁmotive + ṁfeeder + ṁbleed   ·   ρ = pabsolute / (R T)

Air: γ = 1.4, R = 287.05 J/(kg·K), feeder and bleed at 293.15 K. Motive Cd = 0.94 for the British nozzle and 0.82 otherwise. Branch friction follows Reynolds number (laminar, transition and Haaland turbulent closure). Entry, bend and mixing losses remain assumed coefficients, scaled by the loss selector. Native STEP curves supply lengths and diameters; junction continuations are approximate. These eight bodies are not assigned the separate historical British calibration. See validation, holdout errors and exclusions.

Equations, validity and source dimensions

The nozzle uses choked or unchoked compressible flow. The mixing balance conserves gas and powder mass, axial momentum and total energy with co-moving powder inertia. The outlet must match the shared vessel/outlet pressure. A subsonic branch is tried first; an ideal critical-mixing/internal-shock branch is tried for an expanding bore when required. Low-Mach and compressible regimes are identified automatically. Local shock structure, separation, deposition, particle segregation and dense-phase transport remain unresolved.

For very short tubes, the free-jet approximation can fail before a forward solution is found. High powder loading in the feeder also requires an experimental transport check. The original-size British nozzle is 2 mm; the other six nozzles are 3.5 mm. File labels such as “0.75″” are not used as bore measurements.

CAD source: the eight STEP files supplied in this chat. Each filename and SHA-256 fingerprint is retained with the selected case. Length is from the actual nozzle exit to the end of the main mixing bore, excluding the diffuser. British nozzle positions in these files differ from the existing dashboard assembly.

Compressible-nozzle relations: NASA Glenn — mass-flow choking and isentropic relations. These references support the nozzle equations; they do not validate the eductor estimates.

How pressure changes dilution

Compare all eight STEP cases under the same operating conditions. Each point re-solves the pressure and entrainment balance using that case’s nozzle, common feeder, suction branches and outlet.

Air per kilogram of powderR = ṁair / ṁpowderHigher means more dilute.
Powder per kilogram of airλ = ṁpowder / ṁairLower means more dilute.
Powder concentrationC = ρgas λPressure and temperature also change gas density.

Dots mark the current settings; the selected case has a thicker line. Dashed segments use the compressible estimate. Gaps mean no supported solution; they are not zero. Model sensitivity is not experimental validation.

Read the pressure and dilution conventions

The motive slider is pressure above the selected outlet: p₀,abs = pout,abs + Δp. Vessel and outlet always move together. Lowering this shared pressure while holding Δp fixed also lowers the absolute motive supply pressure. In the Exposure Lab, motive pressure is entered directly in bar absolute.

At fixed supply pressure and temperature, choked motive flow is insensitive to further reductions of downstream pressure. Feeder and bleed flows still depend on the solved internal pressures. Higher powder feed can reduce entrainment through the acceleration load; the model therefore re-solves the airflow.

Adding motive or bleed air reduces powder / air. Once the final air stream has entered, a changing diameter changes velocity and concentration per volume, but not the conserved powder / air mass ratio. Branch powder follows the calculated gas split. Deposition and segregation are not resolved in these bulk station estimates.

The physics behind every model

Follow the air from pressure supply to powder transport, then follow individual particles through shear and turbulent collision exposure. The equations below describe the models implemented in this dashboard.

Where the models apply. Rev 2 single-stage, two-stage and British assemblies use solved pressure/entrainment balances. The eight 20Nov cases reuse those closures with their measured geometry. The Exposure Lab now defaults to solving those pressure / entrainment balances. Prescribed flows are an optional sensitivity mode, not an automatically substituted solution.

Revision 2 · flow, transport and local dilution

Common feeder→Individual curved branches→Jet mixing + radial bleed→Diffuser / outlet
Kᵢ = Kjunction + f(Reᵢ)Lᵢ/Dᵢ + Kbend
ṁᵢ / ṁs = (Aᵢ/√Kᵢ) / Σⱼ(Aⱼ/√Kⱼ)

Series resistance in the common feeder is solved together with parallel branches. Compressible restrictions limit the inlet flux at choking. Vessel and outlet share one pressure; internal pressures are outputs.

pbleed = psuction + (pout − psuction)[1 − exp(−xbleed/Lmix)]

Pressure recovery develops over a finite mixing length. The resulting outlet must satisfy mass, momentum and total-energy balances. The normal-shock branch is used only when the subsonic solution cannot match the outlet.

Gη = √(ε/ν) ≠ |∂U/∂r|
ε = 0.9 k3/2/ℓ,   k = 3σ²/2

Small-scale turbulent shear is distinct from the mean velocity gradient. Jet spread is linked to intensity, mixing length and convective Mach. The integrated dissipation has a mechanical-power ceiling.

∫A C(x,r,θ) Ux dA = ṁpowder(x)
C = ρ(ṁpowder/ṁair) × flux-normalized shape

Local concentration varies across the section and enters the collision integral. Bulk powder/air ratio remains constant after the final air inlet. The chart reports the bulk ratio; local concentration is sampled along the 3D particle paths.

Only the historical British 3.5 mm case was used for calibration. The 2.5 mm nozzle is an independent check. See current errors and exclusions. Equations below also document the retained nominal two-stage and legacy reference models.

A live mass balance

Uses the current home-page controls. Colors connect the streams to the equation; the drawing is a schematic.

01 · All geometries

Pressure becomes jet mass flow

Reservoir p₀, T₀→Nozzle CᴅA→Motive air ṁₚ
m˙p=CDAp02γRT0(γ−1)[r^2γ−r^γ+1γ]

r = pback/p₀, r̂ = max(r, r*), and r* = [2/(γ+1)]γ/(γ−1) ≈ 0.528 for air. Forward flow requires p₀ > pback. Below that critical ratio, the nozzle chokes: further lowering backpressure does not increase mass flow at fixed supply pressure and temperature.

The revision 2 pressure balance uses the solved chamber backpressure for the motive nozzle in both low-Mach and compressible regimes. Prescribed mode uses the chosen chamber pressure. All p in this equation are absolute; T is kelvin. Cᴅ is 0.82 for the nominal sharp nozzle and 0.94 for the British nozzle. These are model coefficients.

Related: NASA mass-flow relation.

02 · Every station and stage

Air and powder obey separate balances

Feeder air + powder→Add motive air→Add bleed air
m˙g=m˙s+m˙p+m˙hλ=m˙dm˙g
ρ=pRTU=m˙gρAC=ρλ

s = suction carrier air, p = motive air, h = bleed air, d = powder. Air / powder = 1/λ. Gas density changes local velocity and concentration; after the final inlet, the mass ratio stays constant unless material is lost.

For two stages, the first outlet becomes the second inlet and the second motive stream adds dilution. Mixed total temperature uses mass-weighted inlet gas enthalpies. The compressible branch subtracts gas and powder kinetic energy to obtain static temperature. Powder heat transfer is omitted.

03 · Historical nominal balance

Entrainment closes a pressure balance

Vessel pressure→Feeder losses→Jet momentum→Outlet pressure
peA=S+p1(A−Aeff)+(m˙s+m˙d)vscosθ−(κm˙g+m˙d)m˙gρmA

The colored S term is nozzle momentum plus exit pressure force. The other terms account for chamber pressure, axial feeder momentum and the outgoing gas/powder momentum. κ = β + fDL/(2D), with β = max[1, (D/(2CsL))²], is the implemented mixing/friction closure.

pvessel − p₁ = sign(ṁs)(1+K)ρsvs²/2 + ṁd(vs−vup)/As

The solver searches for suction flow that makes the calculated exit pressure match the outlet. Stage 2 inherits stage 1 gas flow, temperature and the interstage pressure estimate. A failed low-Mach check triggers the automatic compressible estimate. If that also has no admissible root, the condition remains unavailable.

04 · Historical bleed closure and current CAD branches

British bleed and multiport variants

Suction branches→Jet entrainment→Radial bleed→Diffuser
m˙ent(x)=m˙pmax[0,2Csxdeq−1]
Δprecovery=η[1−(A2Ae)2]ρv222

The archived British closure solved feeder and radial-bleed flows together, including annular restrictions, throat momentum and diffuser recovery. The revision 2 balance above replaces this closure for current predictions. Bleed pressure loss is Khρvh|vh|/2. The C–D insert changes areas, losses and the assumed recovery efficiency; it is not a resolved shock calculation.

Current printed/multiport cases solve a common feeder and individual CAD branch restrictions. Branch diameter, length, curvature and Reynolds-dependent friction determine unequal gas shares; powder shares follow those gas fractions. Each STEP supplies dimensions; these CAD loss coefficients have no geometry-specific experimental calibration.

05 · Exposure Lab; solved or prescribed gas flows

From the jet to a turbulence field

Solved / given ṁs, ṁh, pch→Spreading jet b(x)→ε(x,r), ν(x,r)→Shear G(x,r)
b=b0+sxk=32σ2ε=0.9k32ℓG=εν

A spreading Gaussian jet and the section mean conserve gas mass through the bore. Secondary gas and powder enter at the extracted branch junctions. Internal pressure endpoints come from the pressure/entrainment network; the spatial interpolation between them remains a reduced closure.

The integrated dissipation ∫ρε dV is capped by motive mechanical power remaining after estimated outlet kinetic power. G is a dissipation-based shear estimate, not the mean velocity gradient. Blender and STEP views describe geometry. Revision 2 tracks particles in three dimensions through the extracted passage paths and approximate junctions.

Home-page bulk estimates instead use ε ≈ max(Pjet − ½ṁgvjet², 0)/(ρAL) and residence time L/U. They need not equal the spatial Exposure Lab estimates.

06 · Compact spheres; first-contact tracking

Particles lag the fluctuating air

Local air u + u′→Drag response τp→Particle path→Wall / outlet / horizon
dvpdt=u+u′−vpτp+gτp=ρpdp2Cc18μf(Re)

Below Re = 1000, f = 1 + 0.15 Re0.687; above it, f = 0.44 Re/24. Cunningham slip correction Cc = 1 + Kn[1.257 + 0.4 exp(−1.1/Kn)] accounts for rarefaction. Density, viscosity and mean free path respond to local pressure and temperature.

u′next = e−Δt/TLu′ + σ√(1−e−2Δt/TL) ξ

Seeded Gaussian ξ drives correlated fluctuations. Tracking stops at the first wall contact, inlet escape, outlet exit or time limit. No rebound, deposition probability, particle collisions or powder feedback is applied to the motion. The random walk has no well-mixed drift correction.

07 · Shear, residence and wall statistics

Exposure accumulates along each path

Release→G sampled on path→Threshold crossing→Integrated exposure
tq=∫1G≥qGrefdtηq=νrefqGref
Nℓ=qGreftqmin[1,(ηqdp)23]

q is ½ or ¼. Threshold crossings are integrated within time steps. Gref is either the analytical jet maximum at x/D > 1 or the fixed slide reference. Nℓ is an exposure/turnover proxy, not a counted collision or a breakup prediction.

Tracked time includes wall stops and censored histories; outlet transit uses only particles reaching the outlet. The shear ensemble is zero after a track ends, while accumulated quantities retain their final value. Fixed 0–1 chart axes are display limits; values above 1 remain in statistics and exports.

08 · Brownian and inertial turbulent encounters

From particle pairs to accumulated exposure

Local C → nⱼ→Brownian + turbulent kernels→Integrate on each path→First-event probability
Kᴮ = 4πR(Dᵢ+Dⱼ) / [R/(R+√(δᵢ²+δⱼ²)) + 4(Dᵢ+Dⱼ)/(R√(cᵢ²+cⱼ²)))]

The Fuchs transition kernel uses local absolute pressure and temperature, Cunningham-corrected diffusivity D = kᴮTCc/(3πμd), particle thermal speed c = √(8kᴮT/πm), and the Fuchs jump length δ. It approaches continuum diffusion and free-molecular encounter limits.

KT=8πR2R2G215+waccel2

R = (dᵢ+dⱼ)/2. WZW supplies the inertial acceleration variance from both particle response times, the gas fluctuation variance and dissipation. The tracer limit recovers Saffman–Turner. The pair-clustering factor is assumed to be one. Finite-size, non-Stokes-drag and compressible-turbulence conditions are flagged as extrapolations.

Λᵢ = ∫ Σⱼ (Kᴮᵢⱼ + Kᵀᵢⱼ)nⱼ dt
Pᵢ = 1 − exp(−αΛᵢ)

nⱼ = Cwⱼ/(ρparticle πdⱼ³/6). The two mechanisms are added as a reduced rate approximation. Turbulent shear and inertial acceleration are combined as variances to avoid counting turbulence twice. The within-screen subtotal includes Brownian dose and turbulence that meets R/η ≤ 0.1, estimated slip Re ≤ 0.1, turbulent Mach ≤ 0.3 and density ratio ≥ 100. It is not a corrected total or a validation.

α is capture × sticking efficiency. P estimates the first event in a frozen background; it does not predict coagulated mass or final sizes. Growth, depletion, breakup, pair clustering and hydrodynamic collision efficiency remain unresolved. The legacy tracer-only option is retained for comparison.

Fuchs implementation · WZW equations 22–24

09 · Ensembles, percentiles and confidence intervals

More histories reduce sampling error

Independent seeded histories→Mean / median / spread→SE and 95% CI→N/4 → N/2 → N
SE=sNCI95%≈x¯±t0.975,N−1SE

P05–P95 bands describe variation across histories. Mean confidence intervals describe Monte Carlo uncertainty and narrow approximately as 1/√N. Neither quantifies uncertainty in the assumed flow, geometry or collision kernel. The time-dependent intervals are pointwise, not simultaneous bands. The equations shown are the equal-weight limit; unequal branch weights reduce effective sample size.

The lab defaults to 128 histories per size/offset (768 total), with up to 4,096 per group. Branch-stratified histories use powder-flux weights; weighted effective sample size replaces raw N in uncertainty estimates. Median, SD, SE, P99, coefficient of variation, terminal fates and Wilson intervals are available in Statistics. The coagulation page compares prefix means at N/4, N/2 and N; compare seeds as well before judging convergence.

10 · Separate ideal nozzle/shock model

The optional compressible demonstration

Check local Mach / choking→Area–Mach relation→Shock if required→Match backpressure
AA*=1M[2γ+1(1+γ−12M2)]γ+12(γ−1)
M22=1+γ−12M12γM12−γ−12

The additional nozzle/shock solver is bypassed when its estimated peak nozzle Mach is below 0.3 and it is unchoked. Otherwise it solves an ideal quasi-1D nozzle, including a normal-shock position where applicable. The motive nozzle mass-flow law remains available independently.

This demonstration does not solve the eductor entrainment network or supply the particle field. The automatic eductor estimate described below supplies the exposure flow; this separate nozzle demonstration does not. Resolved interfacial mixing, compound choking and geometry-specific calibration remain future work.

NASA normal-shock relations.

11 · Automatic eductor flow estimate

One shared boundary; internal pressure is solved

p vessel = p outlet→Low-Mach screening→Compressible balance if needed
ṁg=ṁp+ṁs+ṁhpA+(ṁg+ṁd)u+Fwall=IinṁgcpT+12(ṁg+ṁd)u2=∑jṁjcpT0j

The default branch is the reduced balance. Bulk Mach ≥ 0.3, appreciable pressure variation or a failed screening check activates the compressible estimate automatically. Motive-nozzle choking alone does not trigger the extended model.

Iin includes chamber pressure force, nozzle pressure thrust and incoming axial momentum. Effective inlet areas include assumed losses. Gas energy accelerates co-moving, pressureless powder; powder heat exchange is omitted. The root first matches a subsonic outlet to the shared reservoir pressure. If that branch fails and the bore expands into a diffuser, a critical branch imposes M = 1 at the nominal mixing bore, then solves an internal normal-shock area to match the same outlet pressure. Across this ideal shock, mass, momentum and total enthalpy are conserved, while total pressure falls. The particle field still smooths pressure; shock-particle dynamics are not resolved. Normal-shock relations (NASA). Two stages also conserve gas mass and total enthalpy across their calculated interface.

Revision 2 separates suction and bleed pressures with a finite mixing-length recovery and individual inlet restrictions. The historical British body has a documented one-case calibration; CAD-body loss coefficients remain uncalibrated. The spatial particle field remains a reduced interpolation. Shock trains, compound choking, incomplete mixing and separation are unresolved, so some settings still return no admissible estimate.

NASA inlet-flow relation · 1D ejector network research. These support the model framework, not validation of its coefficients.

Geometry, closures and coefficients come from this dashboard's implementation. Equations provide estimates; case-specific flow, turbulence, wall-contact and coagulation validation is still required.
